en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
Pādukavagga 66.
The Training Rule on Head-wraps.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one who had his head wrapped. ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I will not teach the Dhamma to one with a wrapped head who is not ill.
One with a wrapped head means:
He has his head wrapped without having shown the hairline.
The Dhamma must not be taught to one whose head is wrapped who is not ill.
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one whose head is wrapped who is not ill, commits an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it was unintentional,
or if there was a lack of mindfulness.
If [the teacher] does not know,
or if he is ill,
and he causes [the student] to uncover the hairline and teaches [the precepts].
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The sixth training rule is finished.
